overview: Alumni Engagement and Fundraising Propensity addresses teams rely on lagging aggregates when forecasts or decisions depend on changing operational conditions in education and research operations. The first proof of value uses event attendance, past giving and consent preferences. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is qualified outreach acceptance rate, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: event attendance, past giving and consent preferences; define qualified outreach acceptance rate and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from University CIO / Academic Program Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including backtest across seasonal and peak periods with a holdout cohort.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for qualified outreach acceptance rate
